mission: Discover intrinsic state-dependent FFN computation and functional redundancy in distilled Wan video generation; reduce actual FFN and total generation cost at preserved free-running video quality. Quantization metadata is optional auxiliary coarse magnitude information, not the default hypothesis source.

questions.name: What useful information exists?
questions.focus: What intrinsic FFN activation, signed contribution, spatial-temporal and downstream-sensitive structure exists; what is known without computing the whole FFN?

questions.name: Can available information pay for itself?
questions.focus: When is a conditional action valuable after acquisition, routing, caching, layout and physical costs versus a matched fixed alternative? Magnitude-only metadata is secondary.

questions.name: Which actual FFN work may be omitted?
questions.focus: Which real W1/GELU/W2 FFN work is conditionally unnecessary, reusable or reparameterizable while preserving residual/attention/trajectory video function and measured native latency?

default_research_loop: Start from the most recent full-hidden/shared-column/quantizer-closure results and discover at least one mechanism-level explanation not reducible to retuning top-k/raster/group64; new mechanisms may originate from intrinsic function, nonlinear algebra, video sensitivity, spatiotemporal organization, or physical computation
Explore competing mechanism hypotheses and PRD reformulations from real source/earlier videos/prior art, including a mathematical counterexample or distinguishing prediction
Ground decision-critical claims in precise Wan FFN W1-GELU-W2-gate-residual/attention/step semantics; isolate quantization-specific observations
Discriminate using proof, source, permitted saved data or a proposed separately authorized finite experiment; keep evidence scope exact
Derive potential FFN work reduction and conditional information price without presupposing proxy, 64-channel grouping, dense restoration, cache or a specific FP4 implementation
